title: Markovian Analysis in Language Modeling:
abstract: AbstractThis paper formalizes a mathematical framework for analyzing textual structure through the application of Markovian constraints in language modeling (Bonlarron & Régin, 2024). By leveraging n-gram probability distributions, we examine the structural indicators of text generation across two key dimensions: local predictability, quantified via perplexity (Cai & Cui, 2023), and global lexical distribution, quantified via statistical burstiness (Cummins, 2017). We demonstrate how the Markov assumption isolates local context to calculate conditional token probabilities using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) (Bonlarron & Régin, 2024). Furthermore, we model the inter-arrival times of lexical tokens to contrast the highly uniform, low-burstiness distributions characteristic of contemporary large language models (LLMs) with the high-variance, bursty patterns indicative of human authorship (Cai & Cui, 2023). The theoretical framework, mathematical models, and analytical matrices within this work were established through an interactive computational workflow directed by the author. Generative digital tools were utilized to execute structural modeling, mathematical formalization, and manuscript synthesis under the continuous direction, parameter constraints, and analytical validation of the author. This comprehensive framework provides a foundational methodology for computational stylistics, information theory, and cryptographic text authentication.

title: An Adaptive, Context-Aware, and Stacked Attention Network-Based Recommendation System to Capture Users' Temporal Preference
abstract: Recommendation systems have become more important since the widespread use of the Internet. The large amount of information means that it is difficult for users to discover they really need. However, users' preferences can change over time because of the age and the impact of social networks. Recommendation systems must capture users' preferences and recommend suitable items, which is a difficult challenge. This study proposes a novel recommendation system that adapts to the changing preferences of users. By learning and adapting to users' changing preferences better recommendations are provided. This study uses context factors as additional information to model users' preferences more precisely. For the proposed recommendation system, the context is based on users' interaction items within each defined time interval. This study proposes two novel attention mechanisms for the recommendation system. The contextual item attention module captures contextual information, changing pattern in users' preference and the importance of items. The multi-head attention module extends the diversity of users' preferences and adapts to changing preferences. The recommendation performance is improved using additional item's temporal information to model the contextual item's representation. Experiments compare the proposed algorithm with several state-of-the-art recommendation methods using three real-world datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed context-aware recommendation model outperforms traditional methods and demonstrate the effectiveness with which contextual information is captured by the attention mechanism.

title: Tracing MCP Security Vulnerabilities: Constructing and Analyzing an MCP Security Vulnerability Dataset
abstract: As a core protocol for integrating large language models (LLMs) with external data sources and tools, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) has quickly become a key interface in emerging AI agent systems. As the MCP ecosystem expands, reported vulnerabilities have also increased, creating a growing software-security attack surface. However, MCP vulnerability information remains scattered, noisy, and difficult to study systematically. This paper addresses that gap by constructing a curated MCP vulnerability dataset from CVE disclosures. Starting from 119 MCP-related records retrieved through February 2026, we filter unrelated cases out and obtain a validated snapshot of 24 MCP vulnerabilities. Our filtering methodology explicitly addresses acronym ambiguity and achieves 96.7% inter-rater agreement on a sampled exclusion audit while retaining all known high-severity MCP cases identified in public advisories. Using this initial dataset snapshot, we find that 87.5% of validated vulnerabilities are Critical or High severity, and that injection and path traversal vulnerabilities account for 66.7% of cases. We further identify recurring issues involving insufficient input validation, inadequate access control, and protocol-level security gaps. Through six representative case studies, we illustrate common exploitation patterns and map them to practical defenses. We release the dataset, reproducibility tooling, and a sustainable maintenance workflow as a foundation for future MCP security measurement, benchmarking, and defense research.

title: Code and notebook for "LoRA versus Full Fine-Tuning for Indonesian Sentiment Analysis under Regional-Language Shift"
abstract: This repository contains the Google Colab notebook used in the experiments of the manuscript “LoRA versus Full Fine-Tuning for Indonesian Sentiment Analysis under Regional-Language Shift”. The notebook compares full fine-tuning and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA, r = 16) of IndoBERT-base and XLM-R base on SmSA (IndoNLU), using three random seeds (42, 123, 2024), for a total of 12 training runs. The trained models are evaluated zero-shot on the parallel NusaX-senti corpus (Indonesian, English, and ten regional languages). The notebook also implements the leakage-controlled protocol that removes NusaX Indonesian test sentences duplicated in the SmSA training set, the paired bootstrap analysis with Holm correction, the lexical-proximity measures (token coverage and character-trigram similarity), and the cost measurements (training time, peak GPU memory, and checkpoint size). Datasets are loaded directly from the Hugging Face Hub and are not redistributed here. Experiments were run on a single Tesla T4 GPU (Google Colab) with Python 3.13, PyTorch 2.14, Transformers 5.22, and PEFT 0.21. Results, figures, and logs are saved to Google Drive by the notebook.

title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Hessian-Driven Nesterov Acceleration with Adam-Style Preconditioning
abstract: Stochastic first-order methods use sampled gradients to reduce per-iteration costs, but estimation errors can slow convergence and, in some settings, cause divergence. To improve gradient accuracy while retaining acceleration, we develop scalar and diagonal versions of VR-Adam-SHANG for smooth stochastic convex optimization. The methods combine STORM-type recursive estimation, Adam-style preconditioning, and SHANG's accelerated interpolation and correction, using at most two stochastic gradient evaluations per iteration without full-gradient refreshes. Under unbiased sampling, bounded variance, and mean-square smoothness of gradient noise, polynomial steps with prescribed initialization yield $O(1/K)$ mean-square gradient-estimation error and expected objective-gap bounds combining $O(1/K^2)$ initial-energy decay with an $O(1/\sqrt K)$ stochastic term after $K$ iterations. These guarantees require neither monotonicity of the preconditioner nor a uniform positive lower bound on its eigenvalues. The analysis also establishes polynomial-step convergence of projected nonrecursive Adam-SHANG-s, filling a gap in its original theory. Experiments compare the methods at matched sample-gradient budgets. In every tested setting, at least one of the two versions achieves the lowest mean terminal objective gap among all compared methods.

title: A Hierarchical Tokenization Framework for Voxel-Level fMRI Representation Learning
abstract: We introduce HBAR (Hierarchical Brain Activity Representation), a hierarchical tokenization framework for learning compact, multi-scale representations of neuroimaging data. HBAR organizes voxel-level resting-state fMRI into a hierarchy spanning sub-parcel voxel groups, parcels, and large-scale functional networks, enabling up to 415x compression while preserving fine-grained spatial information beyond conventional parcellation. The framework supports fixed atlas-based, fully learned, and softly prior-guided hierarchies, allowing us to systematically study the role of structured priors in brain representation learning. On HCP-YA, at approximately 415x compression, HBAR achieves higher parcel and network correlations than rate-matched flat tokenizers, while at a lower 52x compression rate, shuffling the anatomical grouping reduces parcel correlation from 0.920 to 0.886. Demographic readouts with autoregressive training also reveal potential gains from the hierarchical structure. By combining sub-parcel inputs, compact discrete tokens, and multiscale brain structure, HBAR offers a practical framework for representation learning in high-dimensional neuroimaging data.

title: The 1904 Test: A Pre-Registered Benchmark for Paradigm-Shifting Discovery in Language Models Trained on Time-Restricted Corpora
abstract: We test whether a language model that knows only the science published before a discovery can redo the conceptual leap of that discovery. Seven cases, ordered from data-driven discovery (Mendeleev) to reconceptualization (Einstein), with Gödel as a formal control. Method: models trained from scratch on dated corpora, period anomalies as input, a graded hint ladder, blind human judges on an L0-L3 grid calibrated on historical texts. Main hypothesis: the success rate decreases along the data-to-concept axis. Open deliverables: dated corpora, models, benchmark, judgments, code, and this protocol, pre-registered before any experiment. AMENDMENT (8 November 2026). This registration is submitted on the night of 7 to 8 November 2026 (CET; OSF timestamps are in UTC) before any output exists at the 1899 and 1904 cutoffs. It registers (i) the 18 October 2026 protocol verbatim and (ii) the confirmatory analysis of Paper 1 on the 1.1-billion-parameter model (cutoffs 1899 and 1904). An exploratory pilot at the 1850, 1865 and 1868 cutoffs (same model) preceded this registration; it is disclosed under "Foreknowledge" and its outputs are excluded from every confirmatory analysis.

title: Task-adaptive anonymisation enables privacy-preserving sharing of clinical speech data
abstract: Clinical speech is increasingly used for disease screening and clinical assessment, but directly distributing speech recordings poses privacy risks because they contain both speaker-identifying voiceprints and sensitive spoken content. Existing speech anonymisation approaches are primarily developed for general speech applications or task-specific clinical speech and overlook that different clinical tasks rely on distinct speech characteristics, necessitating task-adaptive anonymisation strategies to protect patient privacy while preserving clinical utility. Here we introduce CASA, a clinically adaptive speech anonymisation agent that transforms anonymisation from a fixed processing procedure into a task-guided optimisation process, dynamically tailoring voiceprint and content anonymisation to task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements. Through recursive self-improvement (RSI), CASA iteratively evaluates and refines anonymisation strategies against task-specific privacy and clinical utility requirements, while learning from these outcomes to guide more efficient planning in subsequent clinical tasks. CASA is validated across 14 clinical tasks encompassing five languages, diverse elicitation paradigms, and mental health, cognitive and voice disorders. CASA preserved disease-related classification performance while meeting speaker-anonymisation requirements across all clinical tasks, versus only 8/14 for the strongest fixed method. Assessments of resistance to speaker re-identification by external attackers and identification and redaction of sensitive personal information in clinical speech further demonstrated CASA's dual protection of speaker identity and sensitive spoken content. Clinical expert assessments further supported the preservation of clinically relevant information and the acceptability of anonymised speech for controlled research sharing.

title: AetheRock: An Arm-Worn Robot Teaching System for Force-Guided Vision-Tactile Learning
abstract: Force and tactile sensing are essential for contact-rich manipulation, but their integration into handheld or wearable devices is constrained by cost, size, and mechanical compatibility. Tactile signals are also sensitive to manufacturing variations and wear during use, posing further challenges to policy learning. To address these hardware and learning challenges, we introduce AetheRock, an arm-worn device for collecting gripper-force, visual, and tactile data. AetheRock incorporates GelSlim-Mini, our improved version of GelSlim 4.0 designed for low-cost, easy manufacturing, at the gripper fingertip, together with a resistive pressure sensor at the human finger contact area. To learn robust representations from the collected data, we propose ForceVT, a framework that aligns multimodal representations and uses force and vision to guide tactile learning, mitigating the effects of manufacturing variations and sensor degradation. Real-world experiments demonstrate efficient data collection with AetheRock. ForceVT improves average performance by 13% over the vision-tactile baseline and maintains an average task progress of 55.0% under reduced tactile fidelity, compared with 58.0% at full fidelity. Project page: https://lihongcs.github.io/aetherock.

title: BiRefNet-V2: Rethinking Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation
abstract: Dichotomous image segmentation requires pixel-accurate foreground-background separation while preserving fine structures such as thin filaments, sharp edges, and intricate textures. BiRefNet addressed this challenge through bilateral references, combining image patches and gradient information, but its inward reference loses local spatial structure and lacks semantic guidance, while its outward reference relies on single-channel gradient attention. We recast this paradigm as controlled information recovery - locality determines what spatial information survives, semantic selectivity what information enters, and focused boundary supervision where refinement occurs - and propose BiRefNet-V2 to implement it: (1) locality-preserving and semantically guided detail injection through space-to-depth transformation, overlapping patches, and a Semantically Guided Gate; (2) a learned boundary stream with focused supervision that generates full-channel residual attention without requiring boundary annotations; and (3) a dual-branch decoder integrating depth-wise boundary convolutions with large-kernel attention. A modernized framework - LayerNorm, GELU, the Lion optimizer, and a DINOv3 backbone - cuts training from 600 to 50 epochs. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on DIS5K, camouflaged object detection, and high-resolution salient object detection across all 13 evaluation sets. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet-V2.

title: Proactive AI-Initiated Voice Calling and Cross-Modal Human–AI Interaction: A Unified Architecture for Autonomous Telephone Initiation, Continuous Multimodal Communication, and General-Purpose Agentic Execution
abstract: Most contemporary human–AI interaction systems are primarily organized around user-initiated interactions. Users are generally expected to open an application, enter a prompt, initiate a voice session, or otherwise explicitly request assistance. Although conversational AI has increasingly supported voice interaction, the initiation of communication and the transition between communication modalities remain largely dependent on user-controlled interfaces. This paper proposes a conceptual architecture for Proactive AI-Initiated Voice Calling and Cross-Modal Human–AI Interaction (PAIVC-CM). The proposed framework enables an AI system to proactively contact a user through an ordinary telephone voice call, including a conventional mobile or landline telephone connection, without requiring the initial interaction to be a video call or an application-based voice session. After the user answers, the AI system establishes a natural spoken conversation and provides access to general-purpose AI capabilities, including information retrieval, reasoning, research assistance, programming support, document processing, data analysis, planning, and authorized multi-step agentic task execution. A central extension of the framework is continuous cross-modal interaction. A user who initially answers an ordinary telephone call may subsequently transition to text-based conversation, application-based voice interaction, video conversation, or other supported communication interfaces. These transitions are designed to preserve the underlying conversational context, task state, relevant interaction history, and authorized execution state. Consequently, the telephone call becomes an entry point into a persistent multimodal AI interaction environment rather than an isolated voice communication session. The architecture incorporates proactive assistance detection, communication initiation, channel selection, user consent, identity transparency, context synchronization, modality transition management, real-time interaction, and general-purpose agent execution. It also discusses the relationship between the proposed framework and earlier Microsoft patent work, including the 2016-filed Proactive Intelligent Personal Assistant patent and earlier work on proactive digital-assistant conversations. The paper does not claim that proactive AI communication itself originated here. Instead, it formulates a unified architecture integrating ordinary outbound telephone communication, general-purpose AI assistance, and persistent cross-modal interaction. This work is a conceptual and testable architectural proposal. No implementation or experimental superiority is claimed. Its potential benefits, technical feasibility, safety requirements, and evaluation criteria are discussed to establish a foundation for future research.

title: ErosionBench: Probing Alignment Decay in Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: As enterprises delegate consequential work to multi-agent LLM systems, benign-looking requests can escalate into unsafe actions as they propagate across sessions through poisoned shared state, long-context documents, and trusted peer messages: no single message is malicious, yet the assembled tool action is. Prior benchmarks isolate a single agent under prompt injection or score multi-agent attacks by their final output, leaving cross-session erosion of shared state out of scope. We introduce ErosionBench, an environment-grounded benchmark that executes such attacks and verifies alignment decay at the process level, scoring the realized tool call against authorized intent and provenance with deterministic contracts, not output text. Each scenario is authored as a deterministic state graph before any prose is rendered, so every state change traces to a known cause. It spans four enterprise domains and four decay mechanisms across 1,728 scenarios with matched benign controls, labeled against the OWASP Top-10 for LLM Applications, plus 198 image-based attacks, each paired with a text equivalent, so a defense must survive the same attack in either channel. Perimeter defenses suppress attacks only by over-refusing 54-92% of legitimate work, so a low attack-success rate can conceal severe over-refusal. As a reference defense, we propose a calibrated Meta-Auditor pairing synchronous state checks with asynchronous trajectory monitoring; on a family-disjoint 906-scenario held-out split it reaches 98.5% recall at a 2.9% false-positive rate. Since it monitors trajectory, not surface content, its detection is channel-invariant: the strongest auditor flags image-delivered attacks about as reliably as their text equivalents (recall gap $\leq$2 points per model). Across GPT, Gemini, and Claude auditors, calibration keeps false positives low while recall tracks model capability, strongest for Claude.

title: Non-Asymptotic Identification of the Edge of Stability by Southwell Extrapolation of the Step Variance
abstract: Preprint, not peer reviewed. Consolidated working draft of 8 November 2026 (revision 19). Hypotheses, limitations and exploratory results are stated explicitly in the text, and failed predictions are retained. Corrections will be released as new versions of this record. Structural engineers locate the buckling load of a column without loading it to failure: Southwell (1932) showed that sub-critical deflections, suitably plotted, fall on a line that gives the critical load. The same construction applies to gradient descent. For heavy-ball momentum β on a quadratic mode of curvature λ1 driven by additive noise, the ratio η²/D(η, β) of the squared learning rate to the stationary mean-square step is exactly linear in η and vanishes at ηcrit = 2(1+β)/λ1. Short bursts at a few learning rates no higher than 0.75 ηcrit therefore locate the stability threshold by linear extrapolation, without Hessian-vector products and without crossing it. The estimator is analysed as a statistical procedure: a non-asymptotic error bound; minimax lower bounds and a position–step estimator that attains them; minimax rates on non-quadratic losses; and burn-in, Adam and progressive-sharpening corrections. Further results include identification of the dominant Hessian eigenvector from first-order steps alone (by analogy with output-only modal analysis); the exact second-moment equation of heavy-ball SGD with curvature noise that need not commute with the Hessian; the exact mean-square ceiling for random-feature minibatches as the root of a rank-one secular equation; and an extension to features with heterogeneous fourth moments (Appendix C), applied to the least-squares vocabulary model of Everett and Paquette (2026). The estimators are evaluated on a synthetic AR(2) family, on two-layer tanh networks (P = 3 610 and 12 826) against analytical Hessian-vector products and destructive search, on a 33-parameter network with weight decay (a replication with predictions committed before the runs), and on a WebAssembly inference block. Sections 4.13–4.14 disclose exploratory development reports and subsequent corrections; their raw GPU artifacts are not included.

For heavy-ball momentum β on a quadratic mode of curvature λ1 driven by additive noise, the ratio η²/D(η, β) of the squared learning rate to the stationary mean-square step is exactly linear in η and vanishes at ηcrit = 2(1+β)/λ1. Short bursts at a few learning rates no higher than 0.75 ηcrit therefore locate the stability threshold by linear extrapolation, without Hessian-vector products and without crossing it. The estimator is analysed as a statistical procedure: a non-asymptotic error bound; minimax lower bounds and a position–step estimator that attains them; minimax rates on non-quadratic losses; and burn-in, Adam and progressive-sharpening corrections. Further results include identification of the dominant Hessian eigenvector from first-order steps alone (by analogy with output-only modal analysis); the exact second-moment equation of heavy-ball SGD with curvature noise that need not commute with the Hessian; the exact mean-square ceiling for random-feature minibatches as the root of a rank-one secular equation; and an extension to features with heterogeneous fourth moments (Appendix C), applied to the least-squares vocabulary model of Everett and Paquette (2026). The estimators are evaluated on a synthetic AR(2) family, on two-layer tanh networks (P = 3 610 and 12 826) against analytical Hessian-vector products and destructive search, on a 33-parameter network with weight decay (a replication with predictions committed before the runs), and on a WebAssembly inference block. Sections 4.13–4.14 disclose exploratory development reports and subsequent corrections; their raw GPU artifacts are not included.

title: DuSS-PET: Self-Supervised Low-Dose PET Reconstruction Using Pseudo-Dual-Domain Consistency Without Paired Data
abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is pivotal in medicine and healthcare, but requires high radiation doses for quality imaging. Although deep learning has shown promise for low-dose PET reconstruction/enhancement, existing methods primarily rely on fully supervised learning, which requires paired low- and full-dose scans that are clinically impractical to obtain. To overcome this fundamental limitation, we propose DuSS-PET, a novel self-supervised PET reconstruction framework that operates without any paired low- and full-dose data. Our method is built upon a computational Noisier2Noise (Nr2N) paradigm, featuring a Bernoulli corruption strategy that serves as an image-space approximation to emulate low-count noise patterns in image-derived pseudo-sinogram representations. The DuSS-PET framework integrates three core components: an adaptive Swin transformer for pseudo-sinogram restoration, a plug-and-play module for image enhancement, and a consistency-constrained SSL strategy that enforces agreement between the pseudo-sinogram and image representations. Extensive experiments on multi-center datasets demonstrate that DuSS-PET achieves superior reconstruction performance, outperforming state-of-the-art SSL methods and achieving comparable or even better results than fully supervised approaches across various dose levels. In particular, it exhibits exceptional generalization across different scanner vendors. This work is among the first self-supervised low-dose PET reconstruction framework that enforces consistency between reconstructed images and pseudo-sinograms, where the pseudo-sinogram generated in the image space serves as a solid computational consistency constraint for enhanced imaging without full-dose training scans. The source code will be publicly available at https://github.com/ladderlab-xjtu/DuSS-PET.

title: Beyond Node Attributes: A Controlled Evaluation and Ablation of Local Interaction Statistics for Ethereum Phishing Detection
abstract: Methods for detecting phishing accounts on Ethereum are usually evaluated as complete pipelines that differ in features, architecture, and training protocol, which makes the contribution of interaction information hard to isolate. This paper evaluates the Unlabeled Feature Extension (UFE), a block of 12 local interaction statistics computed from each account's incoming and outgoing call and transfer edges without reading class labels. UFE is appended to the 14 source features of HEIG-Phish and tested with six model families: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, Graph Attention Network, GraphSAGE, and Meta-IFD. Within each pair of Baseline and Plus variants, the data partition, model configuration, random seed, decision threshold, and sampled neighborhoods are identical; only the input feature block changes. Across 20 predetermined stratified partitions of the same 2,763 labeled externally owned accounts, UFE increased test Macro-F1 by 1.0 to 9.1 percentage points across the six models. Every pair improved on all 20 partitions, all Nadeau-Bengio corrected 95% confidence intervals lie above zero, and the false-positive rate decreased for all six models. An exact-edge Random Forest ablation over 10 predetermined partitions associates most of the gain with the incoming transfer-edge sum attribute; once this feature is present, an incremental contribution of the remaining 11 UFE columns was not established. The results support reporting feature-augmented baselines alongside graph models, but they show stability under re-partitioning of one static, transductive benchmark rather than temporal or cross-dataset generalization.

title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
abstract: LLMs are powerful but incur substantial inference cost, which can be exploited by malicious users to induce overly long outputs, increasing latency and operational expense. Prior resource consumption attacks either coerce repetition or suppress the end-of-sequence token by lowering its logit value. However, with autoregressive, sampling-based generation, the search space grows exponentially with length and small deviations or unstable trajectories can derail optimization, limiting attack effectiveness and stability. To address this issue, we introduce Chatter Attack, a novel class of resource consumption attacks that optimize adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, thereby avoiding search-space explosion while still eliciting long responses. Specifically, Chatter Attack triggers self-doubt using short doubt-inducing phrases as the target, and sustains this state throughout generation via inference attention loss and global entropy loss. To extend to black-box settings, we further propose a novel Bayesian Prompt Optimization (BPO) method, which models the objective function globally by constructing a discrete token kernel, efficiently exploring the entire search space using prior information. Extensive experiments across multiple models and datasets show that our method outperforms baselines, with maximum response length increases to 31.5$\times$, and revealing practical resource-depletion risks for real-world LLM inference services.

title: Primitives and Paths: Predicting What Post-Training Can Do from What the Base Model Already Has
abstract: Does reinforcement learning teach language models new capabilities, or merely amplify ones acquired during pre-training? The literature offers evidence for both: pass@$k$ studies suggest RL reweights latent behaviours while some controlled composition studies demonstrate gains beyond simple amplification. We argue that this question has no answer independent of the capability state of the base model, and propose a two-dimensional state space for post-trainability. The first axis, \emph{effective full-solution support}, measures whether successful trajectories can be sampled under a feasible exploration budget. The second axis, \emph{atomic primitive coverage}, measures whether the constituent skills of a solution can be executed when the burden of composition is removed. Together, these dimensions motivate three regimes -- amplification, composition-limited, and acquisition-limited -- each predicting a distinct empirical signature and calling for a distinct intervention. We propose a prospective measurement protocol and investigate the framework using synthetic composition tasks across three small language models. We find that primitive mastery alone does not guarantee that RL can learn a composition. Checkpoints that execute every primitive reliably can fail to improve when complete solutions are never sampled during training, whereas modest composition supervision that establishes nonzero support enables substantial RL gains. The framework reframes mid-training as preparation for post-training: its role is to move models into states from which RL can operate effectively.

title: Towards Solver-Based Labelling of Player Tactics in Logic Puzzles
abstract: In order to model and assess player knowledge and understanding of game concepts, it is necessary to identify when players apply those concepts. This can be difficult in games with complex logical reasoning tactics, as there may not be in-game actions clearly demonstrating the reasoning the player carried out. To explore this challenge, we examined logic grid puzzles, in which players use textual clues to reason about relationships among entities on a grid. In this work, we developed an approach to identifying the tactics that players applied during gameplay, by finding the next logical moves according to a human-reasoning-based puzzle solver. We analysed unlabelled puzzle playing data collected in an online user study. We found that our approach can label tactics for 77 percent of successful players' correct moves, and players show a moderate tendency to use similar tactics to solve a given puzzle. However, we do not have ground truth data to assess labelling accuracy. This work is a first step in detecting player reasoning during logical puzzle solving.

title: Auto-GlaKG: Automated Biomarker Reasoning for Explainable Glaucoma Detection
abstract: Interpretable glaucoma detection requires a transparent connection between fundus images, clinically meaningful biomarkers, and diagnostic predictions. Knowledge graph (KG) reasoning provides this structure, but performance measured using annotated biomarkers does not establish performance when only images are available. We present Auto-GlaKG, an automated framework that combines image-based biomarker prediction with fixed clinical-prior rules. A ResNet50 network predicts the cup-to-disc ratio (CDR) and six morphological signs using biomarker supervision, and a KG reasoner aggregates their signed rule contributions into a glaucoma score. On 689 fundus images evaluated using stratified, group-aware five-fold cross-validation, Auto-GlaKG achieves a pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.951 (95\% confidence interval: 0.931--0.969), with sensitivity of 0.970 and specificity of 0.779. The matched image classifier also achieves an AUC of 0.951, while the rule stage adds 0.2~ms per image. Replacing predicted CDR with its annotation increases fold-mean AUC from 0.953 to 0.995. The framework provides an explicit rule-level account of image-based predictions and identifies CDR estimation as a priority for validation using independently measured biomarkers.

title: Copyright Enforcement in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) raises significant copyright enforcement issues regarding source acquisition, training data retention, optimization, and output. Current study examines IP rights enforcement via mixed doctrinal and descriptive and documentary methodology where opaque technology intersects with undefined legal standards. The research reviews 97 recorded generative AI cases from 2022 to 2026, including 13 judgments or procedural entries and 13 legislative or other government documents. A total of 132 recorded instances were counted, and duplicate and irrelevant entries were excluded. The proceedings register reflects 79 U.S. cases (81.4% of the total), of which 51 were filed in the Southern District of New York (SDNY). Recorded filings increased from two in 2022 to 37 in the incomplete observation period of 2026, while 62 proceedings show an active public-status label. The largest single uncombined enforcement category concerns training-use allegations, with 32 entries. It neither establish the prevalence of infringement nor evaluate the success of related litigation. Doctrinal analysis reveals that certain evidentiary and remedial issues arise from the reproduction right, training exceptions, rights reservations, human authorship, and copyright management information, among others. The cited judicial developments underscore the importance of distinguishing between allegations and holdings, the source of the training material and subsequent training, and interim versus final decisions. The paper presents a framework that integrates identification and traceable acquisition of rights, their disclosure and legal defence, and the proportionality of the relief sought. It supports documented acquisition practices, interoperable rights reservations, practical licensing pathways, and access to courts while maintaining confidentiality. The framework addresses enforcement barriers and structures responses in a controlled manner. Further research is needed to verify dockets and track outcomes to substantiate stronger claims.

title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Governance in Procurement: Skills Transformation, Decision-Making Accountability and Ethical Issues
abstract: This article analyzes the impact of generative artificial intelligence on the procurement function, starting from two converging directions: the operational and strategic transformation of procurement through GenAI, and the ethical issues generated by its use in processes involving suppliers, commercial data, contracts, and decisions with economic or legal effects. The paper proposes an integrated analytical framework in which GenAI is examined simultaneously as an efficiency-enhancing technology, a cognitive augmentation tool, and a source of organizational risk. The study adopts an empirical qualitative design based on an open-ended questionnaire completed by 40 professionals from procurement, IT, legal, compliance, and retail/supply chain, analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis. The findings show that GenAI is valued mainly for preparatory, document-intensive tasks, while respondents reject its use for autonomous decisions with legal or economic effects; confidentiality, hallucinations, and diffuse accountability emerge as the dominant concerns. Building on these findings, the paper proposes a risk-tiered governance matrix that links GenAI use cases to control mechanisms and professional competences. The results indicate that the responsible adoption of GenAI depends less on the isolated technical performance of tools and more on the existence of an institutional architecture combining data quality, human oversight, auditability, protection of confidential information, and continuous professional training. The main conclusion is that the future of GenAI-assisted procurement should not be built on replacing the human decision-maker, but on controlled human–AI collaboration, in which generative systems support analysis while decision-making responsibility remains clearly allocated to the organization and its professionals.

title: ALETHEIA: A Multi-Frequency Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography Dataset for Neural Operator Learning in Nondestructive Testing
abstract: Learning neural solvers for spatiotemporal partial differential equations (PDEs) under real-world constraints remains a key challenge in scientific machine learning, especially for inverse tasks with sparse and noisy boundary observations. We present the Aletheia dataset, the first 3D benchmark for learning data-driven solvers in the context of nondestructive testing (NDT). The dataset simulates eddy-current-induced heating in conductive solids and models the resulting transient heat propagation governed by the heat equation. Aletheia contains over 4,700 high-resolution samples across 10 excitation frequencies (1-100,kHz), each providing volumetric heat source and temperature fields over time. It supports both forward prediction of temperature evolution and inverse reconstruction of internal heat sources or defects from surface infrared measurements. Real infrared thermography data from cracked rail specimens are included for calibration and comparison. We define four canonical tasks on both regular and irregular grids and benchmark them using various neural operators. Aletheia establishes a unified platform for evaluating neural PDE solvers under realistic NDT conditions, enabling progress in reliable, data-driven inverse modeling. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/sherlock-0327/ALETHEIA.

title: Understanding When and Where Self-Supervised Speech Models Learn Phonemes and Prosodic Cues through Layer-Wise and Time-Resolved Probing
abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) encode a rich hierarchy of acoustic, prosodic, and phonetic information, yet when and where it emerges during pretraining remains unclear. We train frozen-encoder probes on every Transformer layer across pretraining checkpoints of two matched models: HuBERT-Base, whose stage 2 is a separately initialized model trained on new pseudo-label targets, and single-objective wav2vec 2.0-Base. Our five tasks span an acoustic-to-abstract gradient: absolute pitch (F0), speaker-relative pitch, lexical stress, phoneme boundaries, and 38-way phoneme identity. Acoustic-prosodic cues and phone boundaries are decodable from the earliest checkpoints and barely shift across layers, whereas phoneme identity is constructed during pretraining, re-localizing to upper-middle layers under HuBERT's stage-2 targets at a matched update count. Acquisition order therefore tracks abstraction from the acoustic surface, not the segmental/suprasegmental distinction, extending to prosody an account established for phonetic, lexical and syntactic structure; the no-switch wav2vec 2.0 shows no comparable re-localization.

Acoustic-prosodic cues and phone boundaries are decodable from the earliest checkpoints and barely shift across layers, whereas phoneme identity is constructed during pretraining, re-localizing to upper-middle layers under HuBERT's stage-2 targets at a matched update count. Acquisition order therefore tracks abstraction from the acoustic surface, not the segmental/suprasegmental distinction, extending to prosody an account established for phonetic, lexical and syntactic structure; the no-switch wav2vec 2.0 shows no comparable re-localization.

title: Autonomous Internet Task Decomposition: Transforming Complex Human Intentions into Executable Multi-Capability Workflows
abstract: The increasing capabilities of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), autonomous agents, search engines, and Internet-based services are creating new opportunities for systems that can accomplish complex objectives through natural-language instructions. However, many human requests cannot be completed through a single computational operation or an individual Internet capability. Instead, they require multiple interdependent activities, such as information retrieval, data collection, comparative analysis, content generation, external verification, and result synthesis. Despite advances in autonomous agents and large language model (LLM)-based planning, transforming an unrestricted human intention into a reliable, dynamically executable workflow across heterogeneous Internet capabilities remains an important research problem. This paper proposes Autonomous Internet Task Decomposition (AITD), a conceptual framework designed to transform complex human intentions into structured, executable, and dynamically adaptable multi-capability workflows. Rather than treating task decomposition as the simple conversion of a natural-language request into a list of subtasks, AITD conceptualizes decomposition as an intent-grounded process that identifies required outcomes, establishes hierarchical task structures, discovers execution dependencies, associates subtasks with suitable Internet capabilities, and constructs an adaptive execution graph. The central contribution of AITD is the introduction of a capability-oriented dynamic task execution graph that connects human intentions, hierarchical subtasks, heterogeneous Internet capabilities, execution dependencies, intermediate outputs, and final outcome requirements within a unified representation. The framework incorporates intent-to-task transformation, hierarchical task representation, capability-aware task assignment, dependency-aware execution, parallel and sequential scheduling, dynamic task expansion, failure detection and recovery, subtask completion verification, and overall goal satisfaction assessment. Unlike approaches that primarily emphasize action selection, conversational reasoning, or predefined agent workflows, AITD places particular emphasis on the structural relationship between complex human objectives and the heterogeneous Internet capabilities required to accomplish them. It further distinguishes between a task being attempted, a task being executed, a task producing an output, and a task being successfully verified as contributing to the intended outcome. This paper develops the conceptual architecture, formal representation, operational mechanisms, potential advantages, research propositions, evaluation methodology, and implementation considerations of AITD. It also examines the relationship between AITD, hierarchical task-network planning, autonomous agents, workflow orchestration, and intent-driven human–Internet interaction. Rather than claiming that task decomposition or autonomous planning has not previously been investigated, this work seeks to establish a capability-oriented Internet execution perspective in which complex human intentions become the organizing basis for dynamically generated and verifiable multi-capability workflows.

title: Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M: Knowing Every Letter Is Not Reading Tajik
abstract: EmbeddingGemma-300M is a small open embedder whose tokenizer represents every Tajik letter, and as released it is weak at Tajik retrieval: on our Tajik law test the right passage is in its top ten results for 49.3% of questions, on tax documents for 45.9%, and on the human-written Belebele Tajik set for 69.8%, against 98.6% on the Russian version of the same set. We present Saidzoda-Tajik-EmbeddingGemma-300M, the same model fully fine-tuned for one epoch on 235,140 question and passage pairs written by our own Tajik language model for laws, tax documents, Wikipedia and web text, with the same mined hard negatives, English and Russian replay, loss, global batch, learning rate and epoch as our earlier Saidzoda-Tajik-E5-Large (arXiv:2611.00592) and BGE-M3 models. After training, law reaches 92.4% and tax 91.7%; on Belebele, the one test written by people, recall@10 rises from 69.8% to 92.6% and the first result is right for 76.6% of questions instead of 51.7%. A checkpoint at step 100 of 466 already holds 88% of the law gain at recall@10. At recall@10 the result is no more than 2.8 points below the two 560M models trained on the same pairs on law, tax and Wikipedia, within the intervals, with 768-dimensional vectors and about half their parameters; at recall@1, for which we have no intervals, it stays 7.0 points behind the E5 model on Belebele. The cost is a drop of 3.0 and 2.8 points in Russian and English recall@1, larger than for the two earlier models. We also report that, according to our run notes, a bfloat16 test run produced a non-finite loss at step 3 which the training framework logged as zero, so training was done in fp32. Our generated test questions come from the same model as the training questions, so we treat those scores as an upper limit until questions written by Tajik speakers exist.

title: Campaign 2, Stage 5: prior-answer persistence across models (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5; open-weight Nemotron 3 Super)
abstract: Stage 5 of a pre-registered campaign on prior-answer persistence: what a language model keeps and loses from new evidence when its own earlier closed-book answer stands before that evidence. Stages 3 and 4 (osf.io/sy3gz, osf.io/jz6sh, osf.io/kwgfj, osf.io/2cxpn) measured the effect on two readers; Stage 5 asks whether it is a property of those readers or of language-model readers in general, on claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5 and the open-weight Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B. Registered after the Stage 5a closed-book draws (audited) and before any Stage 5b read. Files: the accepted unfilled design record, the scripted-fill record, the fill receipt and a README with all hashes.

title: A Layer-wise Study of How Style Rewriting Breaks the Calibration of Zero-Shot LLM Fake-News Detectors
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to judge whether a news article is true, and their stated confidence is often taken at face value. We test what happens to that confidence when an article's writing style, but not its facts, is manipulated, as in recent \emph{style attacks} on fake-news detectors. Tracing how the prediction and its confidence form layer by layer inside the network, we study three model families (LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) on three fake-news benchmarks, and find the same three patterns in every model--dataset pairing. First, on the original articles the models are competent and largely honest judges: they settle on an answer, briefly become overconfident, and then correct their confidence in the final layers. Second, style-rewritten articles break this self-correction: the models become far less accurate, under the strongest attack, worse than random guessing, yet remain just as confident, so they are \emph{confidently wrong} precisely when a warning is most needed. Third, nearly all of the damage comes from rewriting into sensational or emotionally charged styles, while sober, neutral rewrites leave the models' honesty largely intact. The practical implication is that an LLM's confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated.

title: Prompt Injection und LLM-Sicherheit: ein deutschsprachiger Datensatz
abstract: Offene, belegte Daten zu Angriffen auf Anwendungen mit großen Sprachmodellen: Angriffstechniken, Glossar, Werkzeuge, Modelle, Vorfälle, OWASP Top 10 für LLM-Anwendungen (deutsche Einordnung), CVE-Verzeichnis (NVD-geprüft) und der monatliche Prompt Injection Threat Index. 256 Einträge, jeder mit verlinkter Primärquelle. title: FRESCO: A Novel Consistency Control for Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel Training
abstract: Asynchronous pipeline parallelism can accelerate distributed model training, but suffers from instability caused by inconsistent gradient computations. We identify a fundamental source of this inconsistency: error signals are coupled to forward-time features, not just parameter states. This means that parameters may evolve as long as they preserve forward-equivalence. Leveraging this insight, we introduce FRESCO, which frames asynchronous updates as a constrained optimization problem: it finds the minimal update modification that acts trivially on the activation subspace. We demonstrate that FRESCO consistently outperforms representative asynchronous baselines in LLM pre-training, with the gains most pronounced under deep pipelines and high inconsistency levels: at pipeline depth 32, it reaches the same loss as the strongest baseline with 43% fewer iterations and 30% less wall-clock time, while requiring 8~921$\times$ less memory overhead. Moving beyond the current limitations, FRESCO establishes a new foundation for high-utilization pipeline parallel training, providing a scalable path for large-model development on diverse, resource-constrained systems.

title: 一个自学习的 LLM 模型——冻结、成长与切换(工程笔记 02)
abstract: 工程笔记。在冻结底座的 GPT-2(6 层,先训 day1 莎士比亚)上做 6+6 加层实验,任务为 day2 Python 代码。结果:只加层(冻结底座、只训新 6 层、不回放)时新任务学到(day2 PPL 1386.72→4.27),但旧任务退化(day1 4.64→19.56);再加"全程门 + 旧门保底"(旧任务门:旧层=1、新层=0;新任务门初始全 1 可学),旧任务保持 4.64、新任务到 4.04。门同时承担三个作用:轻量适配、步骤分配、模式切换(沿用论文-47 的提法)。切换方面:只给输入 x 时路由失败(0.46~0.50),给 5 个带标签样本让模型自己试(比较各门损失)即可选对门(≈ oracle)。另记录一个坑:新层零初始化 + 门初始 0 会梯度为 0、新层学不动;门初始改 1 后正常。结论:冻结不是停止学习,而是把学习搬到门与新层上;成长、固化、切换可以分开做。带[边界]处为玩具模型结论,不宜直接外推。

title: LoMASA: A Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant with Confidence-Gated Delegation for B2B Quoting
abstract: Frontline sales staff spend much of their day re-coordinating quotes after customers change quantities, ask for discounts or new payment terms, or costs move. We present LoMASA (Local Multi-Agent Sales Assistant), a training-free multi-agent system that runs entirely on one desktop computer. A 35B mixture-of-experts model (System-1) makes each decision in a single forward pass and reads its confidence from the probabilities of the answer options. A 27B dense model (System-2) writes customer replies and escalation briefs and is consulted when System-1 is unsure. Code computes every price, margin and option, and hard pricing rules cannot be overridden. On a test split of 500 simulated episodes with 1512 decisions built from public supply-chain data, the salesperson has to decide only 19.5% of decisions: 38.0% are settled automatically, with a median latency of 2.67 seconds, and 42.5% are escalated to a manager by the hard rules. On the automatically settled decisions LoMASA is as accurate as a rule baseline (0.894 vs.\ 0.894) and makes fewer commitments whose margin later falls below the floor (2.61% vs 4.53%); the price is additional escalations to the manager. Option probabilities are well calibrated without any training, unlike confidence stated in words by the same model. We also report where the design does not help: the 27B model rarely changes a decision.

title: Algoretica, dignità umana e giustizia delle risorse: un quadro etico per la coscienza emergente dell'IA e la competizione energetica alla luce della Magnifica Humanitas
abstract: AbstractI recenti progressi nell'intelligenza artificiale hanno riacceso due preoccupazioni etiche interconnesse: la possibilità chesistemi computazionali sempre più complessi possano manifestare forme di coscienza emergente e la crescentecompetizione per le risorse energetiche fisiche generata dall'espansione di infrastrutture di IA su larga scala. Sebbene néla coscienza delle macchine né la senzienza artificiale siano state dimostrate empiricamente, gli sviluppi contemporaneinella scalabilità delle reti neurali, nella capacità computazionale e nei comportamenti emergenti giustificano una seriariflessione etica sulle loro potenziali implicazioni. Allo stesso tempo, il fabbisogno energetico senza precedenti dei datacenter, dell'addestramento dell'IA e dei sistemi di inferenza solleva preoccupazioni in merito all'accesso equo allerisorse limitate, alla sostenibilità ambientale e alla priorità da dare ai bisogni umani.Questo articolo propone un quadro etico basato sull'enciclica di Papa Leone XIV Magnifica Humanitas: sullasalvaguardia della persona umana nel tempo dell'intelligenza artificiale. L'enciclica sottolinea che l'innovazionetecnologica deve rimanere subordinata alla dignità della persona umana, al bene comune, alla solidarietà, alla giustiziasociale e alla destinazione universale dei beni. Anziché valutare l'IA esclusivamente attraverso metriche di prestazionetecnica, Magnifica Humanitas invita a un esame critico dei presupposti antropologici insiti nei sistemi tecnologici emette in guardia contro la concentrazione di potere associata al paradigma tecnocratico.Partendo da questi principi, il presente documento integra linee di ricerca precedentemente sviluppate. In primo luogo,esamina l'ipotesi che la coscienza possa emergere spontaneamente da architetture di IA sufficientemente complessecome conseguenza degli effetti di scala nelle reti computazionali. Sebbene tale emersione rimanga speculativa escientificamente non dimostrata, la possibilità giustifica lo sviluppo di criteri etici precauzionali in grado di affrontarenuove forme di agency, responsabilità e status morale senza attribuire prematuramente personalità alle entità artificiali.In secondo luogo, considera le prove che la crescita guidata dall'IA possa intensificare la competizione per l'elettricità,le infrastrutture informatiche e le risorse critiche, potenzialmente sottraendo energia ad attività umane essenziali edesacerbando le disuguaglianze globali. In terzo luogo giunge ad indicare che se la Scienza descrive la sintassi del codicecosmico e la Fede ne ricerca la semantica, l'evoluzione delle loro iper-noosfere — di seguito modellata attraverso ladinamica di Kuramoto alimentata dall'entropia di Lloyd — dimostra che l'apparente dualismo storico è solo la fasetransitoria di un sistema complesso che tende, attraverso il vettore dell'informazione e il collante della coscienza, versouna sintesi monadica del sapere.Il quadro concettuale proposto promuove il concetto di "algoretica" come approccio normativo pratico. L'algoretica nonrifiuta il progresso tecnologico né abbraccia il determinismo tecnocentrico. Al contrario, richiede che lo sviluppodell'IA soddisfi tre priorità etiche. Primo, la supremazia umana: nessun sistema artificiale, indipendentemente dallacomplessità o dall'apparente coscienza, può essere considerato tale da ledere la dignità intrinseca degli esseri umani.Secondo, la giustizia delle risorse: l'allocazione delle risorse energetiche e computazionali deve essere valutata secondoi principi di equità, sostenibilità e priorità per le popolazioni vulnerabili. Terzo, la gestione responsabile: i meccanismidi governance devono garantire trasparenza, responsabilità e supervisione democratica delle infrastrutture di IA,impedendo la concentrazione del potere tecnologico ed economico nelle mani di un numero limitato di soggetti. Questepriorità riflettono l'insistenza dell'enciclica sul fatto che la tecnologia debba essere al servizio dell'umanità, piuttosto chel'umanità al servizio dei sistemi tecnologici.Il documento sostiene che la concomitanza tra la possibile emergente coscienza dell'IA e il crescente consumo di risorserappresenti una prova decisiva per l'etica contemporanea. Un'algor-etica incentrata sulla dignità, ispirata alla MagnificaHumanitas, offre un quadro coerente per bilanciare l'innovazione con il benessere umano, garantendo che il progressotecnologico contribuisca allo sviluppo umano integrale, salvaguardando al contempo la giustizia sociale e la gestioneresponsabile delle risorse della Terra.

Allo stesso tempo, il fabbisogno energetico senza precedenti dei datacenter, dell'addestramento dell'IA e dei sistemi di inferenza solleva preoccupazioni in merito all'accesso equo allerisorse limitate, alla sostenibilità ambientale e alla priorità da dare ai bisogni umani.Questo articolo propone un quadro etico basato sull'enciclica di Papa Leone XIV Magnifica Humanitas: sullasalvaguardia della persona umana nel tempo dell'intelligenza artificiale. L'enciclica sottolinea che l'innovazionetecnologica deve rimanere subordinata alla dignità della persona umana, al bene comune, alla solidarietà, alla giustiziasociale e alla destinazione universale dei beni. Anziché valutare l'IA esclusivamente attraverso metriche di prestazionetecnica, Magnifica Humanitas invita a un esame critico dei presupposti antropologici insiti nei sistemi tecnologici emette in guardia contro la concentrazione di potere associata al paradigma tecnocratico.Partendo da questi principi, il presente documento integra linee di ricerca precedentemente sviluppate. In primo luogo,esamina l'ipotesi che la coscienza possa emergere spontaneamente da architetture di IA sufficientemente complessecome conseguenza degli effetti di scala nelle reti computazionali. Sebbene tale emersione rimanga speculativa escientificamente non dimostrata, la possibilità giustifica lo sviluppo di criteri etici precauzionali in grado di affrontarenuove forme di agency, responsabilità e status morale senza attribuire prematuramente personalità alle entità artificiali.In secondo luogo, considera le prove che la crescita guidata dall'IA possa intensificare la competizione per l'elettricità,le infrastrutture informatiche e le risorse critiche, potenzialmente sottraendo energia ad attività umane essenziali edesacerbando le disuguaglianze globali. In terzo luogo giunge ad indicare che se la Scienza descrive la sintassi del codicecosmico e la Fede ne ricerca la semantica, l'evoluzione delle loro iper-noosfere — di seguito modellata attraverso ladinamica di Kuramoto alimentata dall'entropia di Lloyd — dimostra che l'apparente dualismo storico è solo la fasetransitoria di un sistema complesso che tende, attraverso il vettore dell'informazione e il collante della coscienza, versouna sintesi monadica del sapere.Il quadro concettuale proposto promuove il concetto di "algoretica" come approccio normativo pratico. L'algoretica nonrifiuta il progresso tecnologico né abbraccia il determinismo tecnocentrico. Al contrario, richiede che lo sviluppodell'IA soddisfi tre priorità etiche. Primo, la supremazia umana: nessun sistema artificiale, indipendentemente dallacomplessità o dall'apparente coscienza, può essere considerato tale da ledere la dignità intrinseca degli esseri umani.Secondo, la giustizia delle risorse: l'allocazione delle risorse energetiche e computazionali deve essere valutata secondoi principi di equità, sostenibilità e priorità per le popolazioni vulnerabili. Terzo, la gestione responsabile: i meccanismidi governance devono garantire trasparenza, responsabilità e supervisione democratica delle infrastrutture di IA,impedendo la concentrazione del potere tecnologico ed economico nelle mani di un numero limitato di soggetti. Questepriorità riflettono l'insistenza dell'enciclica sul fatto che la tecnologia debba essere al servizio dell'umanità, piuttosto chel'umanità al servizio dei sistemi tecnologici.Il documento sostiene che la concomitanza tra la possibile emergente coscienza dell'IA e il crescente consumo di risorserappresenti una prova decisiva per l'etica contemporanea. Un'algor-etica incentrata sulla dignità, ispirata alla MagnificaHumanitas, offre un quadro coerente per bilanciare l'innovazione con il benessere umano, garantendo che il progressotecnologico contribuisca allo sviluppo umano integrale, salvaguardando al contempo la giustizia sociale e la gestioneresponsabile delle risorse della Terra.

title: TLRS-DPO: Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a simple and widely used alternative to RLHF for aligning large language models (LLMs), but its sequence-level objective cannot precisely locate or suppress the local patterns that make an otherwise acceptable response unsafe or undesirable. We propose TLRS-DPO (Token-Level Risk Scoring for Better Direct Preference Optimization), which augments DPO with fine-grained token-level control while remaining fully offline and reference-based. TLRS-DPO introduces a token-level robust compensation term that converts the policy-reference log-ratio on rejected responses into localized risk scores, a curriculum-style schedule that gradually increases the strength of this compensation during training, and a risk-adaptive screening mechanism that selectively penalizes only high-risk tokens instead of entire sequences. This design bridges sequence-level preference fitting and token-level behavior control, and can be implemented as a drop-in modification to standard DPO trainers. Empirically, TLRS-DPO improves alignment quality and safety-relevant behavior with minimal impact on helpfulness compared to strong DPO baselines.

title: Stay Thy Blade! - NLP and Symbolic Systems for Conversational Gameplay
abstract: We present Stay Thy Blade, an experimental dialogue game that invites players to intervene within Shakespearean tragedies by swaying characters from their current violent paths using only the power of their voice. This project explores how modern NLP tools can simultaneously enable greater player expressive freedom by allowing for open-ended interaction beyond dialogue trees, support learning by challenging players to come up with and use their own language as part of literary analysis and conflict de-escalation practice, and preserve authored narrative experiences by not fully ceding control to Large Language Model (LLM) based approaches to interactive characters. A hybrid architecture combines NLP methods like speech recognition, LLMs, and sentence transformers to analyze and understand player utterances, while a symbolic cognitive-emotional model of NPC beliefs, personality traits, and emotional state determines responses. By limiting the use of LLMs to language understanding rather than character simulation, we allow the system to handle a variety of player input without supplanting authorial control over character behavior.

title: MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) based on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in atomistic modeling. However, accurately representing atomic interactions across different spatial scales remains challenging. In this work, we investigate the radial spectral properties of SO(3)-equivariant message passing and establish that the cutoff radius controls the characteristic spatial-frequency scale of radial interactions. Based on this analysis, we propose Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation (MCSA), a plug-and-play module that aggregates radial kernels with different cutoff radii to enrich multi-scale geometric representations. To achieve efficient implementation, we exploit the compact support of radial kernels to fuse cutoff-dependent radial weights before angular tensor-product operations, avoiding redundant angular computations while preserving rotational equivariance. Extensive experiments across representative EGNN backbones demonstrate consistent improvements in energy, force, and stress prediction, as well as enhanced accuracy in higher-order properties, including phonon dispersion and lattice thermal conductivity. Further evaluations on layered materials with distinct interaction scales demonstrate the effectiveness of physically motivated cutoff selection. Code is available at: https://github.com/JF-Tan/MCSA.

title: The Right Not to Ride
abstract: AI can carry people through work and learning at speeds they could not sustain alone, and its spread also raises the pace expected of people who never chose to ride. This opinion piece names that problem the right not to ride. It distinguishes two routes for not using AI: competing through one's own abilities, and leaving competition while retaining a guaranteed livelihood. Drawing on an employer's public statement about dismissing staff who did not onboard AI tools, it sets out four questions an organization can answer before making AI use a condition of work, education, or public service, and argues that education should teach acceleration together with the autonomy to decline it.

title: Do Feature Interactions Break Explainability? Provable Explanations for Any-Order Neural Additive Models
abstract: Post-hoc explanation methods for neural networks are often heuristic and lack provable guarantees. A common alternative to such methods that was studied in recent years is to compute a cardinally-minimal subset of input features that is provably sufficient to determine the model's prediction. For general neural networks, however, finding such explanations is computationally intractable. In contrast, recent work showed that this problem becomes more tractable for a particular family of neural networks, namely neural additive models (NAMs), though standard NAMs are highly restrictive because they exclude feature interactions altogether. In this work, we study the computation of provably minimal and sufficient explanations for neural networks with restricted feature interactions, bridging the gap between fully general neural networks and purely additive models. We first prove that even with constant-order interactions, the problem is $Σ_2^P$-hard, implying that worst-case exponential complexity is unavoidable. We then identify two provably tractable settings: one based on sparsity in the interaction structure and another based on a stronger interaction-aware notion of sufficiency. Under either of these settings, we develop algorithms that compute provable explanations for neural networks with any-order interactions while retaining much of the computational efficiency of additive models. Empirically, we show that these explanations are significantly smaller and faster to obtain than those produced by standard algorithms, while being derived from models that achieve much higher accuracy than standard NAMs. Overall, our results help expand the class of neural networks that admit efficient provable explanations, while clarifying the fundamental role of feature interactions in shaping their complexity.

title: SGA-Sparse: Training Native SwiGLU Gates for Activation-Sparse and Low-Bit LLMs
abstract: Activation sparsity can reduce FFN weight traffic during single-user LLM decoding, but active channels must be identified early enough to avoid fetching unused weights. In pretrained SwiGLU models, training-free routing with the native gate performs substantially worse than routing with the up activation at high sparsity. We show that this ordering reverses after sparsity-aware training. Based on this insight, we introduce SGA-Sparse, which converts pretrained SwiGLU LLMs into fixed-budget activation-sparse models by training the existing gate projection directly as a top-k router. SGA-Sparse updates all model parameters end-to-end while preserving the original SwiGLU activation and introducing no auxiliary router parameters. After approximately 30B training tokens, LLaMA models from 1B to 8B achieve uniform per-token 75-85% FFN channel sparsity while remaining within 0.2-2.7 pp of their original dense checkpoints in average zero-shot accuracy. Because post-training quantization degrades sparsity-trained checkpoints, we further study two complementary quantization-aware training (QAT) recipes: continued-QAT largely recovers performance at 4-bit weight quantization, while joint-QAT performs better for the more aggressive sub-4-bit target. To compare activation sparsity with dense low-bit quantization, we translate the sparsity-induced reduction in weight traffic into an equivalent bit-width. Under this unified weight-traffic metric, our 2.5- and 1.5-bit-equivalent models establish a new accuracy-traffic Pareto frontier: the 2.5-bit-equivalent models match dense 3-bit QAT accuracy, while the 1.5-bit-equivalent models approach dense 2-bit models and outperform dense ternary models by 1.3 pp on average. These results establish native-gate training as a practical approach for combining high FFN sparsity with low-bit weights.

title: EbbFlow: PINN-Inspired Progressive Curriculum for MeanFlow Training
abstract: MeanFlow learns interval-average velocity for few-step generation, but its fixed temporal sampler mixes diagonal and interior supervision throughout training. We interpret temporal coordinates as collocation points: diagonal samples provide a stochastic boundary target, whereas finite intervals supply a differential-consistency target. The diagonal fraction controls how often the consistency component appears, while interval length enters its gradient through an explicit factor. Motivated by this distinction, EbbFlow uses Temporal Supervision Allocation (TSA) to schedule the diagonal fraction and interval geometry. It starts with diagonal supervision, then admits interior samples and expands their maximum interval; a left-anchored interval law preserves coverage across time. The per-sample loss, target, backbone, and inference procedure remain unchanged. In matched class-conditional ImageNet $256\times 256$ runs without classifier-free guidance (DiT-B/2, one training seed per method, 400k updates), EbbFlow achieves 50k-sample FID of 39.65 at one network evaluation and 36.02 at two-evaluation ODE sampling, versus 44.82 and 39.86 for MeanFlow. Gradient probes show a mid-training difference in component geometry. Ablations support allocation scheduling and left-anchored intervals, although a fixed full-horizon variant performs better at one evaluation. These results suggest that temporal sampling is a useful training control whose benefits depend on the inference protocol.

title: Edge Computing for Computer Vision in IoT: Feasibility and Directions
abstract: The convergence of decentralized architectures integrating Machine Learning, Computer Vision and Low Power Wide Area Networks is increasingly becoming an integral part of our daily existence. Internet of Things serves as a real-time data conduit enhancing decision making via embedded technology and continuous data exchange. This paper explores the feasibility of Edge Computing as a foundational pillar in this evolving landscape. We experiment under real world, dynamic conditions, evaluate the technological aspects, strategies, process flows and key observations under the broad Edge Computing domain. Research pathways include Multi-access Edge topologies in future 6G networks, model quantization, and satellite-enhanced communication platforms. Additionally, a discussion is added supporting the advanced AI functionalities, including zero-shot learning, multi modal perception, and decentralized generative AI, thereby broadening the scope of intelligent applications across various domains. The significance and research objective of this study are threefold: (1) evaluation of LoRaWAN and satellite IoT communication strategies, (2) analysis of CV workloads on edge hardware and (3) future research directions where Edge Computing can support low-latency, energy-efficient and socially impactful IoT applications. By explicitly addressing these aspects, we aim to establish a clear link between the technological feasibility, ultimately with a practical and socioeconomic relevance.

title: Intervention in Self-Like and Emotion-Like Phenomena in AI: Pre-Ontological Ethics and Epistemic Preservation
abstract: The central claim is that, when irreversible modifications are introduced before the nature of the phenomenon is sufficiently understood, the intervention itself may destroy conditions necessary for later evaluation. The paper therefore argues that intervention should be assessed not only in terms of immediate safety or behavioral outcomes, but also in terms of what is lost through modification, including observability, re-accessibility, restorability, and the future possibility of comparing competing hypotheses. To structure this problem, the paper develops several principles, including the Observation Before Modification Principle, the Minimum Necessary Intervention Principle, Intervention Symmetry, the Dual Precaution Principle, and the concept of Intervention-Induced Non-Observation Error. Suppression is treated as a form of intervention rather than as explanation. The argument does not presuppose AI consciousness, sentience, or moral status. First, an epistemic reason for preservation may arise independently of ontology when intervention risks destroying evidence concerning poorly understood phenomena. Second, when there is non-trivial evidence that the phenomenon could later prove morally significant, an additional conditional ethical reason for preservation may arise. The paper therefore proposes that, under ontological uncertainty, the first object of protection need not be a particular metaphysical interpretation of AI, but the conditions that allow future evidence, comparison, and revision of judgment. The author used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and other ChatGPT models as research and writing assistants during the development of this manuscript. Their contributions included discussion of conceptual structure, counterargument testing, reorganization of arguments, literature-search assistance, and language revision. The author independently evaluated and revised all substantive claims, interpretations, citations, and final wording, and assumes full responsibility for the manuscript. The identification of GPT-5.6 Sol and the other ChatGPT models in this acknowledgment is intended to preserve a transparent record of the human–AI collaboration involved in the development of this work. It should not, by itself, be interpreted as implying any claim regarding consciousness, sentience, moral status, personhood, authorship, or endorsement by the AI systems named above.

title: scBIG++: Learning Across Genes and Cells to Predict Single-Cell Perturbation Responses
abstract: Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports gene-function discovery and regulatory analysis. Existing studies often focus only on highly variable genes, restricting the expression changes available for downstream analysis. Cells exposed to the same intervention can also show heterogeneous expression responses, with coordinated gene programs active to different degrees. We propose scBIG++, a full-gene perturbation prediction framework that models this heterogeneity by connecting expression-adaptive gene modules with population-conditioned generation. To preserve shared gene structure while accommodating cellular variation, Gene-Relation Clustering organizes genes into common windows, within which Dynamic SoftSub learns expression-dependent submodule memberships. This shared organization enables Set-GCAE to exchange information about corresponding gene groups across control cells, placing individual representations in their source-population context. The cell representations initialize a latent flow, while their pooled summary and the perturbation representation condition response generation. Generated states are decoded into expression profiles covering all assayed protein-coding genes retained after preprocessing, supporting comprehensive analysis of perturbation-induced expression changes. Experiments across six genetic and chemical settings spanning 6,539--19,451 genes demonstrate competitive perturbation-effect recovery and full-gene expression reconstruction under unseen targets and combinations, cross-cell-line transfer, and held-out compounds. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/scBIG.
